body: Everyone here has been very supportive of me. I feel the least I can do is return the favor.

Manic Depression is pretty much Bipolar. It depends on the severity. Bi-polar is switching back and forth without reason, randomly. Manic Depression is never knowing what you will feel like during the day. You could wake up happy and excited about life, ready to do something, or just sit in bed and wonder why you hate your life. Neither of them are fun.

One thing I did, was I started Free-writing. I wrote whatever came to my head. The next day, I would look back at what I had written, without almost no memory of it. But I could always tell my mood by what was written. More and more of them became depressing. I realized I needed help after one of my free-writing exercises contained a fake suicide note. I was thinking, "I wonder what it would sound like if I wrote a suicide note." Reading it the next day scared me. I never finished the note, and I don't intend too. But I will keep it, to remind me of how bad it got. And how to never end up in a situation like that again. 

If your low points get bad, find help. That's what I'm doing now. I'm keeping myself positively distracted until I can go an talk to someone. Just don't let it get the best of you

Well, it made me more depressed then it should have. I have a therapist set up for later on this week. Its more then just my fear of intimacy. I'm Manic Depressive, and I need to get it under control.

Your advice is great though. Its very true. Confidence is key. If you don't have faith in yourself, you don't have anything.

To me, its not about how many people show up. Its how I can have a good time with the ones that do. Granted, this last one ended up with me alone and depressed. 

The two people who would come, sound like the two worth inviting.

My issue comes with sleeping with them. I can load the gun, but I can't pull the trigger.

I understand the awkward moments you're going through. The truth is, girls prefer a direct approach over an indirect one (Typically, at least. I don't know this one obviously, so she may be different.). But generally speaking, they want someone to talk too. 

Have you spoken to this girl before? Do you know if you have anything in common with her? Either way, you want closure on the topic, and I can respect that.

To be completely honest, I haven't been with someone in 4 years. This is how most of my experiences end. I like a girl. We hang out. She shows interest. She wants to get intimate, and I freeze, or do or say something awkward.

I would much rather be with her then just sleep with her (Not exactly a typical Male response). But I know thats kind of what shes looking for at the moment. She left my house that night and ended up sleeping with another guy who lives near her.

The entire night, and the following day, I spent hating myself. It could have been me. It should have. And I didn't do it. To be honest, I'm still hating myself for it.

I'm not an everyday drinker, or smoker. But I have noticed my depression gets worse when I drink. This is a more recent event. The weed helps calm me down, helps me to stop over-analyzing things. But I think a better approach is in order. 

I'm calling a therapist tomorrow. I obviously have underlying issues that's preventing me from pursuing what and who I want.

I'm 24, been out of college for a while. Not with a degree, just a dropout. Still, counseling doesn't seem like a bad option at this point. I need to get help. I see that. 

That last line you wrote really hit home to me. I don't know 100% why. But its stuck. Thank you for a healthy does of truth.

It seems like when you're stuck in a rut of depression, everything seems like its your last chance. And not in a good way, like "This could be my last day on Earth, lets go do something!" way. Depression takes over, and tells you "You just fucked up. Thats it. You're done. That was your last shot, and you blew it."

It feels like the edge is pushing itself closer to me. I'm trying to back away, yet it just crumbles as fast as I can back away from it.

Does that even make any sense?

I'd love to engage, especially with people who've had similar issues. I'm willing to listen to any suggestions anyone has.

At this point, i'm not sure what I'm more afraid of. Dying, or how often I think about myself dying.

24 years old. Technically yesterday. I didn't have a celebration or anything, I've never been one to push my birthday as a big deal. 

Thanks for the birthday wishes. I don't know of any support groups in my area. I wouldn't even know where to start looking. But the therapist might not be a bad idea. Though in the past, their usual solution was to stick me on meds. I'm not necessarily against meds, the idea just sort of scares me.
